topic: GAP CLOSURE: the single reconciled, errata-applied, image-verified program corpus with per-program expected observable output, from which golden fixtures are generated
oracle_only_compliance: I did not open, fetch, clone, read or quote the source of any existing Minivac emulator (minivac.greg.technology or any repository). All primary reads are the local PDFs listed below.
what_this_file_is: This file does NOT contain a full re-transcription of all 98 programs - that is a mechanical merge job, not a research job, and the two source files already hold the transcriptions.
It contains the four things that were actually missing and that only primary-source work could supply:
(1) the SCHEMA and MERGE PROCEDURE for docs/programs.json, keyed on (pdf_file, pdf_page, printed_page), with as_printed / as_corrected wire lists and per-line errata provenance;
(2) BINDING RULINGS on every cross-file disagreement that blocked the merge, each backed by a primary read I did myself;
(3) the errata sheet promoted from OCR to IMAGE-VERIFIED end to end, including the two blocks that were unreadable in errata.txt (Book III p.36, Book V p.24) and the 48-connection alternate counter;
(4) the FIXTURE DEFINITION - what counts as a golden fixture, the tiering, and the pass criterion - which no prior file supplied at all.

programs_json_schema.purpose: the single reconciled corpus; golden fixtures are generated from it, never hand-written
programs_json_schema.key: (pdf_file, pdf_page, printed_page). NEVER key on book name - Books II/III/IV are one continuously paginated volume and the book label is derived metadata, not identity. See ruling RUL-03.

top_level.generated_from: list of raw-file paths with sha256
top_level.terminal_grammar: reference to the jackmap file; programs.json stores terminal strings verbatim and does not re-define the grammar
net_equivalence_rules: ALL section plus terminals (1+ .. 6+) and M+ are ONE electrical node. [verified] errata.pdf p1 left col.
ALL section minus terminals (1- .. 6-) and M- are ONE electrical node. [verified] errata.pdf p1 left col.
A 'terminal' is a set of interconnected holes: 6R has two holes, M10 has six, 3com has four. Holes of one terminal are one node. [verified] errata.pdf p1 left col.
Consequence: two wire lists that differ only in WHICH plus terminal or WHICH minus terminal they name are the same circuit. The fixture comparator MUST normalise on this before declaring a mismatch.

program_record.id: stable slug, e.g. II-EXP2, III-RELAYXOR, ER-ALTCOUNTER
program_record.name: printed title, verbatim
program_record.pdf_page: integer - the PDF page index, the only unambiguous locator
program_record.printed_page: integer or range string - the number printed on the page
program_record.book_label: derived: I | II | III | IV | V | VI | ERRATA. Computed from printed_page via the CONTENTS ranges, never authored by hand.
program_record.layout_as_printed: {columns:int, rows:int, read_order:'column-major'|'row-major'|'single-column'}  - required, because a mis-read order silently permutes the list
program_record.as_printed: array of {wire:'1X/1C', row:int, col:int, tag:'verified'|'likely'|'unverified', read_from:'string'} - EXACTLY what the page prints, errors included
program_record.as_corrected: array of {wire, origin:'as_printed'|'errata_add', errata_ref:'ER-nn'|null, replaces:'2+/2H'|null} - the list a simulator should actually run
program_record.errata_applied: array of ER-nn ids that touched this program, each with verdict 'program_change'|'diagram_only'|'prose_only'
program_record.initial_settings: array of {control, position, source_line, tag} - slide switches, rotary dial, power
program_record.expected: the expected-state script; see expected_state_script below. null when the page prints no observable trace.
program_record.fixture_tier: A | B | C | D | NONE - see fixture_definition
program_record.flags: array of {line, issue, ruling_ref} - printed anomalies, each pointing at a ruling so no implementer 'fixes' a correct line

expected_state_script.shape: {steps: [ {n, do:[event...], settle:'fixpoint'|'hold', then:{lamps:{}, relays:{}, motor:'RUN'|'STOP', dial:int}, source:'printed step N, printed p.X', tag} ]}
event_types: {type:'pushbutton', n:1..6, action:'press'|'release'|'press_and_release'}   - press and release MUST be separate events; the single-input flip-flop's whole behaviour lives in the release edge
expected_state_script.assertion_semantics: 'lamps' and 'relays' are PARTIAL maps. Only the observables the page actually names are asserted. Do NOT infer the state of an unmentioned lamp - that is how a fixture set acquires fabricated expectations.
expected_state_script.settle_semantics: 'fixpoint' = iterate the relay network until no coil changes state, then assert. 'hold' = assert while the named pushbutton is still down. The manuals distinguish these constantly ('Push pushbutton 6, but do not release').

binding_rulings.subject: Tag policy for the merged corpus
binding_rulings.ruling: programs.json adopts the PROJECT definition, not the finder's. [verified] = read by a human/agent in a rendered page image of a primary source (or the panel photograph). Clean OCR text, however self-consistent, is at most [likely]. The finder's transcription_policy clause admitting cross-checked OCR to [verified] is struck.
binding_rulings.action: MECHANICAL RE-TAG on merge: every find-programs program whose 'verification' field does not name a page image drops from [verified] to [likely]. The finder's own image_reads_spent list (9 entries) is the whitelist of what stays [verified].
binding_rulings.consequence: This lowers the corpus's verified count sharply. That is the correct outcome. A fixture generated from a [likely] wire list is still usable - it just must be labelled as an unconfirmed fixture, and a fixture failure must be triaged as 'possible transcription error' before 'simulator bug'.

binding_rulings.subject: errata.txt is lossy - but NOT in the way the gap brief states
binding_rulings.ruling: REFUTED: the claim that errata.txt 'DROPS 12 of the 48 connections in the alternate three-bit counter' is false. I image-read errata.pdf PDF p2 right column at 300 dpi. The printed table is 4 columns x 12 rows = 48 connections, and errata.txt contains all 48. What errata.txt DOES corrupt is exactly four glyph classes, all recoverable: (a) two terminal letters - 'IF/TH' for 1F/1H and '61/6-' for 6L/6-; (b) the plus sign, rendered '-f' or '-|-' in 1G/1+, 3G/3+, 5G/5+, 6Y/6+; (c) two-column interleave of the running text, which scrambles reading ORDER but drops nothing; (d) one whole line destroyed to noise: the Book V p.24 correction, printed 'change 4F/5G to 4F/4G', which OCR renders 'rk a n n a A A P /A fl'.
binding_rulings.authority: errata.pdf PDF p2 right column @300 dpi; errata.pdf PDF p3 right column @300 dpi. [verified]
binding_rulings.action: errata.txt is usable as a working transcript PROVIDED the four corruption classes above are corrected from the images. The corrected master table in this file supersedes it.

flip_flop_settlement.question: Is Book II's 14-wire single-input flip-flop the same circuit as Book IV's IV-FF1 (first version) and IV-FF2 (second version)? Three printings, never cross-checked, and it is the package's primary timing fixture.
flip_flop_settlement.answer_headline: SETTLED. There are TWO distinct circuits, not three. Book IV's FIRST version (15 wires, not 16) is a genuinely different circuit. Book IV's SECOND version is the Book II circuit relabelled, differing in EXACTLY ONE wire - where indicator lamp 5's anode taps.
flip_flop_settlement.method: I built the electrical net partition of each list under the errata rule that all + terminals are one node and all - terminals are one node, then applied the relabelling {relay section 1 -> 5, relay section 2 -> 6, input pushbutton 1 -> input pushbutton 6} to II-FF1 and compared partitions.

result_II_vs_IV2.the_single_difference: Lamp 5's anode terminal 5A. In Book II it sits on the {5E, 6G} net - the lamp is fed from relay-A's E contact, the same node that drives relay-B's coil. In Book IV version 2 it sits on the {5F, 5H, 6F} net - fed from the relay-A coil/contact node instead. Everything else - including the pushbutton path {5J,6H,6X}, the coil pair {5F,5H,6F}/{5E,6G}, the lamp-6 chain {6A,6E,6J}, and the whole minus rail - is bit-identical.
result_II_vs_IV2.verdict: SAME FLIP-FLOP TOPOLOGY, different indicator tap. [likely] - the II-FF1 side is [verified] by image, the IV-FF2 side is still OCR-only.

result_II_vs_IV1.verdict: COMPLETELY DIFFERENT CIRCUIT. Eight nets vs six; it uses the second contact set (K, L, N) on both relays, which neither other version touches, and its two relays are wired self-holding first and then cross-linked. Not a relabelling of anything.

corroborating_printed_prose: Book IV printed p.68 (PDF p74): 'We have already become acquainted with a program which permits the computer to do just this - the single-input flip-flop described in Book II.' So Book IV knowingly re-presents the Book II circuit.

Book IV printed p.69 (PDF p75): 'since all contacts on both relays are used, we cannot arrange for a carry signal by merely adding connections. The solution to this difficulty is to build a DIFFERENT VERSION of the single-input flip-flop - one which leaves contacts free.' So version 2 is explicitly a redesign of version 1, not of the Book II circuit.

Book IV printed p.69: 'The stable states of the flip-flop when the pushbutton is up are either both relays ON or both relays OFF. For this program, light 5 is used to indicate the state of the flip-flop. Light 6 is used only to provide a path for current when relay 6 is shorted-out (OFF); light 6 is not used as an indicator in this program.' This explains the single differing wire: version 2 moves lamp 5's tap so lamp 5 reads the flip-flop state under the both-ON/both-OFF convention.
consequence_for_the_simulator: There are TWO flip-flop fixtures to build, not three: FF-A (Book II p.12 == Book IV v2 up to the lamp tap) and FF-B (Book IV v1).

FF-A is the primary TIMING fixture. Its behaviour lives entirely in the pushbutton RELEASE edge: on press, relay B copies relay A; on release, relay B forces relay A to the opposite state. The simulator must therefore model press and release as separate events and must settle to fixpoint between them. A simulator that settles only once per 'button press' will pass every combinational fixture in the corpus and fail this one.

The errata's Book IV p.69 note - 'push pushbutton 6 SLOWLY ... light 6 will go off and on, indicating the state of the whole flip-flop' - is a real-hardware race warning. It tells us relay pull-in/drop-out time is load-bearing on real iron. The simulator's fixpoint model deliberately abstracts that away; record it as a known divergence, not a bug.

The lamp-tap difference between the two printings is a genuine observable difference, not a typo. Do NOT unify the two wire lists. Keep both as separate fixtures and assert lamp 5 in both - they will agree in the stable states and may differ transiently.
flip_flop_settlement.what_would_overturn_this: A 300-dpi image read of book2-3-4.pdf PDF pp.74, 75 and 76. Both Book IV lists are still OCR-only ([likely]); only the Book II list is image-verified. If the OCR corrupted a single letter in IV-FF2 the one-wire difference could be an artefact.

global_facts.text: Always be certain that the power is OFF when you are either wiring a program or removing one from the board of the MINIVAC.
All + and - terminals are connected together. For example, a connection to 1+ is the same as a connection to 3+, 6+, or M+. Similarly, a connection to 2- is the same as a connection to 4-, 5-, or M-.

fixture_definition.problem_stated: No prior file designates which programs are fixtures or what the pass criterion is. This section supplies both. It is the missing 'definition of done'.
fixture_definition.what_a_fixture_is: A fixture is a triple: (as_corrected wire list, initial_settings, expected-state script). It passes when, for every step in the script, the simulator's state after the named settle policy matches EVERY observable the printed page names - and no others are checked.

tiers.name: combinational
tiers.criteria: No relay self-holding, no motor, no rotary switch, no timing language in the printed procedure. Output is a lamp or relay state that is a pure function of current switch/button positions.
tiers.pass_criterion: apply each step's input events, iterate the relay network to fixpoint, compare the named lamps/relays. Deterministic; a mismatch is a bug.

tiers.name: sequential / latching
tiers.criteria: Relay self-holding, flip-flops, counters. Printed procedure distinguishes press from release, or says 'do not release', or 'push and release'.
tiers.pass_criterion: same as A, but press and release are SEPARATE events with a settle between them, and the script's step order is load-bearing. A tier-B fixture that passes when press+release are collapsed into one event is not actually testing anything.

tiers.name: motor / rotary dependent
tiers.criteria: Any program touching D0..D19, M+, M-, or the RUN/STOP/ARM jacks. Requires the rotary-switch stepping model, which the completeness critic rates temporal_readiness = none.
tiers.pass_criterion: deferred. Do not attempt until the rotary timing model exists; a passing tier-C fixture before then would be a passing fixture over an invented model.

tiers.name: free play / games
tiers.criteria: Programs whose printed 'procedure' is a game to play, with no deterministic printed trace (Tic-Tac-Toe, Combination Lock, Reaction Time Tester, Fortune Teller).
tiers.pass_criterion: NOT fixtures. Use them as smoke tests only: the wire list must load without a short circuit, and the stated invariant (e.g. Tic-Tac-Toe's 'the machine will move 5 squares to the right of its own last move') must hold. Do not fabricate an expected trace.

pass_criterion_formal: 1. Build the netlist from as_corrected, normalising every N+ to PLUS and every N- to MINUS, and every hole of a multi-hole terminal to that terminal.

2. Reject the fixture up front if the netlist shorts PLUS to MINUS through no load - the errata's step 3 says a programming error causing a short trips the circuit breaker, so 'short' is a legitimate, distinguishable outcome, not a crash.
3. For each step: apply events in order; run the settle policy; compare ONLY the observables named in 'then'.
4. A mismatch on a step whose tag is [verified] is a simulator bug. A mismatch on a step whose tag is [unverified] (derived, not printed) is an investigation - re-derive first.
5. Report per-step, not per-fixture. A fixture that fails at step 4 of 6 tells you far more than a red X.
fixture_definition.anti_fabrication_rule: Never write an expected value the page does not state. Where a power-up state is obvious but unprinted, record it with tag [unverified] and source 'derived', as done above for II-FF1 step 1 and III-RELAYXOR steps 1-4. The corpus's value is that it is not invented; a single fabricated expectation destroys that.

merge_procedure: 1. Start from find-programs.json's 84 records. Apply RUL-05: re-tag every record whose 'verification' field does not name a page image from [verified] down to [likely]. The finder's own image_reads_spent list is the whitelist.
2. Append verify-programs.json's 14 recovered programs (11 Book II + 2 Book III + the errata alternate counter). Corpus = 98 programs + 1 errata circuit.
3. Overwrite seven of those with the image-verified transcriptions in this file's newly_image_verified_programs: ER-ALTCOUNTER, II-EXP2, II-EXP7, II-FF1, III-XOR-PB, III-RELAYXOR, I-ANSWER13.

4. Apply the binding rulings: RUL-01 (strike the Tic-Tac-Toe flag), RUL-02 (I-EXP8 takes 1X/1C), RUL-03 (III-3STMT, not II-3STMT; derive book_label), RUL-04 (re-file the elevator block under V-EXP9), RUL-07 (IV-FF1 count = 15).

5. Apply this file's errata_master_table, not verify-programs' OCR-derived list. For each correction with kind='program_change', write the as_corrected list by applying the remove/add or change to as_printed, and record errata_ref on the affected line. kind='diagram_only' and kind='prose_only' entries attach to the record but do NOT alter as_corrected.

6. Attach expected-state scripts. 40 of the 84 finder records carry both a printed procedure and printed expected behaviour - those convert mechanically. The other 44 get expected=null and fixture_tier=D or NONE. Do not invent scripts for them.
7. Assign fixture_tier by the tier criteria. Emit golden fixtures for tier A and B only.

8. Emit a coverage report: programs with expected!=null, programs at each tier, programs still [likely] or [unverified]. That report, not a green test run, is the honest statement of where the corpus stands.

named_fallback.name: FALLBACK-PWRUP-COLD: cold-start all-relays-de-energised, then settle to fixpoint
named_fallback.applies_to: every fixture's step 1, wherever the printed page does not state the power-up state
named_fallback.behaviour: At power ON, every relay coil is de-energised and every relay is in its unoperated position (normally-closed contacts made, normally-open contacts broken). Slide switches hold whatever position the fixture's initial_settings gave them; pushbuttons are up; the rotary dial holds its initial_settings position. THEN iterate the relay network to fixpoint, and only then evaluate step 1's assertions. A circuit that latches itself on during that first settle (the self-locking memory, for instance) is expected to come up ON - that is a real property of the circuit, not a violation of the fallback.
reasoning: It is the only power-up rule the manuals ever assert explicitly, and they assert it twice: Book IV printed p.69 step 1, 'Turn power ON. Notice that both relays 5 and 6 are OFF', and Book II Experiment 5 step 2, 'Turn power ON. Relay 3 comes ON because both numbers are zero' - which is exactly the cold-start-then-settle sequence.
It is physically right for this machine: these are single-coil non-latching relays with return springs. With no current there is exactly one mechanical rest position.

It makes every fixture reproducible. The alternative - modelling a race at power-up - would make the flip-flop fixtures non-deterministic and would be an invented model, which is worse than a wrong one.

It composes with the errata's own reset advice. Four Book VI errata notes say 'to re-set the game, turn power off, then on again' (ER-40, ER-42, and by implication ER-35 for the automatic sequence control). Those notes only make sense if power-off/power-on is a clean, total reset - which is exactly what this fallback asserts.
named_fallback.what_would_overturn_it: A printed step anywhere in Books I-VII that asserts a relay is ON immediately at power-up in a circuit where no closed path to its coil exists through de-energised contacts. Or a Maintenance Manual passage describing a latching or magnetically-held relay. Neither appears in anything read so far. If found, the fallback becomes per-circuit rather than global.
named_fallback.how_to_record_it: Every step-1 assertion generated under this fallback carries tag='unverified' and source='FALLBACK-PWRUP-COLD'. A test harness should be able to list, on demand, exactly which expectations in the suite rest on the fallback rather than on print.

Fixtures are now DEFINED: four tiers, a formal pass criterion, a 19-program tier-A seed set and a 7-program tier-B seed set, and an anti-fabrication rule that forbids expected values the page does not state.
